title: Match ID Type
description: Identifier types for audience match reporting. Combines hashed PII types (from audience-member.json field names) with token types from uid-type.json, including publisher-scoped PAIR identifiers.

enumDescriptions.hashed_email: SHA-256 hashed email address (matches audience-member.hashed_email). Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — unsalted SHA-256 of the email namespace is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries; treat as PII. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.
enumDescriptions.hashed_phone: SHA-256 hashed phone number in E.164 format (matches audience-member.hashed_phone). Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — unsalted SHA-256 of the E.164 namespace is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries; treat as PII. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.
enumDescriptions.pairid: Publisher Addressable Identity via IAB Tech Lab PAIR. The OpenRTB profile uses User.eids[].source pair-protocol.com, EID.mm 3, EID.matcher set to the publisher's canonical ads.txt ownerdomain, and uids[].atype 3. The URL-safe Base64-encoded KsKp Publisher Identifier must be interpreted with that matcher scope. It is stable across a publisher's advertiser matches only within a Ks key epoch; Ks rotates every 30 days, and current and prior Publisher Identifiers can overlap during rollover. TMP identity objects do not carry matcher or ownerdomain, so a bridge requires an authenticated out-of-band binding to preserve PAIR scope.
